candidates: South Slavic oblique personal pronoun forms built on nj- (njega, njemu, njoj, njih, nje), especially after prepositions, likely firing on an internal subtoken boundary within the pronoun.

Boundary feature for nonstandard pronoun-internal splits, especially English gender-inclusive slash forms like s/he and his/her, with possible secondary firing on tokenization boundaries inside South Slavic pronoun forms such as nje-ga / nje-mu / nje.

Token-boundary / segmentation feature for short pronoun-like forms containing an internal break marker, including slash-marked gender alternations (s/he, his/her) and tokenizer-induced internal splits in inflected pronouns such as njega/njemu/nje.

results.hypothesis: The feature fires on punctuation or clitic boundaries inside gender-inclusive or pronoun-splitting forms such as "s/he", "his/her", or French elision "l'installer".

Each s/he pronoun split looks awkward in print.

Each pronoun choice looks awkward in print.
French learners often misread installer at first.

results.hypothesis: A polysemantic boundary feature for internal splits in short function-word/pronoun forms: either slash-marked alternations in English (s/he, his/her) or subtoken splits inside inflected South Slavic pronouns (njega, nje, njemu).
